If you choose to use more/less than 6 different PNGTubers, you'll need to increase the value in the parameter filters to match the new value associated with that PNGTuber's "PNGberyloaded" parameter. In the case of a seventh PNGTuber, the value for "PNGberyloaded" would be 7.

[THIS PARAMETER IS VERY IMPORTANT]
Increase this parameter as you add more pngtubers. By default, it is configured to support up to 6 different PNGTubers. If you have less than 6 PNGTubers, reduce the range to match it to your amount. The count starts from 1. The value 0 is used when you want there to be no active PNGTubers. Start by setting up your first PNGTuber on the blue node block to the right as it is connected to the <PNGberyloaded> = 1 value.

It is checked when someone redeems the PNGTuber and swaps the active PNGTuber to the one defined by the chosen parameter. It also checks to make sure not to give back the PNGTuber that is currently active. If a duplicate PNGTuber is rolled, it will randomize this parameter again until a non-duplicate is chosen.

The triggers below run to ensure that only the currently chosen PNGTuber graphics are being displayed as defined by the <isspeaking> and <isblinking> parameters. It checks the parameter and hides the logical states associated with every other iteration of that parameter value. This is how the nodegraph knows what to show when you are speaking and not blinking, not speaking and blinking, and so on.

The information produced by these triggers is sent out to the specific PNGTuber setups to the right.

You can use these websocket commands to interface with your streamdeck or app of choice to trigger specific PNGTubers. It is configured to support up to 6 different PNGTubers by default.

You could also connect channel redeem nodes in addition to where the websocket commands nodes are attached to let chat trigger specific PNGTubers!

Set the audio input to the microphone you would like to use.

You can control the sensitivity of voice detection by increasing or decreasing the volume value.

These parameters control the following (1 is yes, 0 is no): : Determines if the camera is currently zoomed in on the PNGTuber. : Determines if a PNGTuber is currently active and which one. 0 is used when no PNGTuber is currently active. : Determines if you are currently beyond the mic threshold to trigger the speaking PNGTuber states. : Determines if your PNGTuber is blinking. : Compares with the last active PNGTuber and ensures selection randomization since the last time it was redeemed (available if the chat redeem is configured). --------------------------------------------
V2.6 VNyan PNGTuber features:--------------------------------------------

- Fully documented with descriptive directions on how to configure and info on how 		parameters function.
- Supports 6+ different PNGTuber graphic sets (you can even add more).

- Supports PNGTuber collision with all VNyan objects.

- Supports smart randomization of PNGTubers via chat redeem. It will remember 			which PNGTuber was used last and always give a different one on the next 		redeem usage.

- Supports zoom in on speaking.

- Supports randomized blinking.

- Supports websocket calls to trigger specific PNGTubers.

- Supports websocket call to activate a closeup view while maintaining expected 			PNGTuber behavior.

- Requires only VNyan to function with included logic for custom SFX.

- Supports a nifty graphical transformation effect when swapping between PNGTubers. 	This effect is also easily editable to suite your needs.

- Supports the triggering of custom graphical VNyan effects based on which 			PNGTuber is currently active.

- Lightweight!

- Easily tweaked and reconfigured to suit your needs.

- Includes an option to trigger a pause function for the currently active PNGTuber

- Designed by a wolf. UwU

You can use these websocket commands to interface with your streamdeck or app of choice to trigger specific camera behavior. The websocket command in black called "PNGZoomOn" lets you zoom in close with another camera if you set one up as a close up. The other websocket command called "PNGZoomOff" returns you to the neutral PNGTuber position.

Hi there! Ever wanted to run your PNGTuber natively in Vnyan? Well, now you can! This logic loop will not work properly unless you configure a few things to support it. Here's what you'll need to get started. Important information is color coded with black nodes: 1. Import 4 "states" of pictures as props that your PNGTuber will use. Currently the node blocks beside this one are set up to support states as follows: - TOP ROW: eyes closed and mouth open - 2ND ROW: eyes open and mouth open - 3RD ROW: eyes closed mouth closed - BOTTOM ROW: eyes open mouth closed align the props to the world but do not lock them to always face the camera. You'll need to mess with the offest in the prop import menu to get placement just right. 2. Setup your mic input and number of active PNGTuber sets. You can do this by looking below this message box. 3. Setup your cameras. The first one can be whatever fits your placement best, and the second is a slightly more "zoomed in" version of the same camera. You will swap between these two cams when you speak to help give your PNGTuber a bit more life. By default, the nodegraph treats "Camera 1" as the idle camera and assumes you'll be situating your PNGTuber in the bottom right hand corner of the screen. "Camera 10" triggers when you are speaking and assumes a camera placement that is slightly more zoomed in than "Camera 1" Below this message box are config options to configure the nodegraph to fit with your particular Vnyan setup. Your camera setup may differ and you may need to change the cameras specified. 4. Go to the settings menu and click on Misc (this is also where you can setup and save your camera). - You'll need to setup a new position for your vtuber as we flatten and shrink it to serve as a source of colliders for other redeems. - Leave the default position slot as is, but go to slot Pos 1 and turn on the gizmo to move around your avatar's base coordinates. - You might have to zoom out to see the gizmo (it looks like the standard XYZ rotational sphere controls in blender). - Make sure to set it as "show" in the same menus you tweak your positions settings). - update all the Load Avatar node below this messgae box with your appropriate VTuber files. This is necessary for your PNGTuber to have collision OPTIONAL STEP 5: - A node block is available below this one that allows you trigger transformations between different active PNGTubers using websocket commands! - A node block is also available below this one that controls the transformation effect. It supports sound but you'll need to load your own files. It can also be tweaked as needed. - Another node block is available beside the other two that lets you specify specific effects to activate when specific PNGTubers are active. An experimental one is provided for you to try as an example. - You can also set up a third camera to use with the parameter and as a zoomed in "close up" cam. - If you're trying to switch between a PNGTuber and your VTuber and notice that your VTuber is missing, scale your hip bone to 1 using the "bone scale" node when your vtuber is active. - ALWAYS restart VNyan to clear parameters after setting up your PNGTuber. Data stored in these may prevent the graph from working as intended without a clean boot after setup. Have fun! There's probably more I forgot, but these are the big ones. Let me know if you have questions and I'm happy to help, I'm best reached on Discord (Berymuch), but you can also message me on Bluesky :3
